newsitem.title: USA: Median CPI rose 0.1 pct in August -- Cleveland Fed.
newsitem.headline: Median CPI rose 0.1 pct in August -- Cleveland Fed.

text.p: The median Consumer Price Index rose 0.1 percent in August versus a 0.3 percent increase in July, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland.
Median CPI is a measure of core inflation, calculated by the Cleveland Fed based on data from the Labor Department's monthly CPI report.
In August median CPI grew at a 1.5 percent annual rate, the bank said. Over the past 12 months, median CPI advanced 3.0 percent, it said.
Earlier, the Labor Department reported CPI rose 0.1 percent overall in August. Excluding volatile food and energy prices, the "core rate" also rose 0.1 percent.
